title: One-to-Many: Posts
description: Add a Post model with a foreign key to User and write endpoints to create and retrieve posts.
problemStatement:
# One-to-Many: Posts

Extend the previous application with a `Post` model that has a foreign key to `User`. Define:
- `id` (Integer, primary key)
- `title` (String, not nullable)
- `content` (String)
- `user_id` (Integer, ForeignKey to `users.id`, not nullable)
- `created_at` (DateTime, default now)

Add a relationship to `User` so that you can access `user.posts` and `post.user`.

Implement the following async CRUD functions:
- `create_post(db, post_data, user_id)` – create a new post for a given user.
- `get_posts_by_user(db, user_id)` – fetch all posts of a user.
- `get_post(db, post_id)` – fetch a post by id, including the author.
- `update_post(db, post_id, post_update)` – update a post.
- `delete_post(db, post_id)` – delete a post.

Write FastAPI endpoints to:
- Create a post (authenticated, using dependency to get current user).
- List posts for the authenticated user.
- Get a specific post (ensure only author or admin can view).
- Update/delete post (only author).
hints:
Add `relationship` on User and Post with `back_populates`.
Example: `User.posts = relationship("Post", back_populates="user")` and `Post.user = relationship("User", back_populates="posts")`.
Use `selectinload(Post.user)` or `selectinload(User.posts)` to load relationships efficiently.
For authorization, check `current_user.id == post.user_id` before allowing update/delete.
expectedOutput: The API allows users to create and manage their own posts. The database stores posts with correct foreign key relationships.
solutionCode:
# models.py additions
from sqlalchemy import ForeignKey
from sqlalchemy.orm import relationship

class User(Base):
    # ... existing columns
    posts = relationship("Post", back_populates="user", cascade="all, delete-orphan")

class Post(Base):
    __tablename__ = "posts"
    id = Column(Integer, primary_key=True, index=True)
    title = Column(String, nullable=False)
    content = Column(String)
    user_id = Column(Integer, ForeignKey("users.id"), nullable=False)
    created_at = Column(DateTime, default=datetime.utcnow)

    user = relationship("User", back_populates="posts")

# crud.py additions
async def create_post(db: AsyncSession, post_data, user_id: int):
    db_post = Post(**post_data.dict(), user_id=user_id)
    db.add(db_post)
    await db.commit()
    await db.refresh(db_post)
    return db_post

async def get_posts_by_user(db: AsyncSession, user_id: int, skip: int = 0, limit: int = 100):
    result = await db.execute(select(Post).where(Post.user_id == user_id).offset(skip).limit(limit))
    return result.scalars().all()

async def get_post(db: AsyncSession, post_id: int):
    result = await db.execute(select(Post).where(Post.id == post_id))
    return result.scalar_one_or_none()

# endpoints.py
@app.post("/posts/", response_model=PostResponse)
async def create_post(post: PostCreate, current_user: User = Depends(get_current_user), db: AsyncSession = Depends(get_db)):
    return await create_post(db, post, current_user.id)

@app.get("/posts/")
async def list_my_posts(current_user: User = Depends(get_current_user), db: AsyncSession = Depends(get_db)):
    return await get_posts_by_user(db, current_user.id)
